To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the SFC-constraint can be transformed into a simple constraint that can be handled by any shortest path algorithm; (2) the maximum achievable flow under SFC-constraint is a fraction of the original network maximum flow; (3) the VNFs can be placed such that the cost is minimized, and the original maximum flow can still be achieved under SFC-constraints.

(1) the SFC-constraints can be transformed to reduce the computational complexity of shortest path algorithms, (2) we develop an efficient combinatorial algorithm to solve a special case of the SFC-constraint maximum flow problem, (3) we formulate the VNFs' placement problem as an ILP problem and prove its NP-hardness.

(1) We present a novel approach to find the SFC-constraint shortest path in a graph by transforming the graph to minimize the number of nodes to visit; (2) we propose a combinatorial solution to the SFC-constraited maximum flow problem; and (3) we show that VNFs placement is NP-hard and propose an ILP formulation.
